thread:
emma: Heads-up — enterprise customer pushed back. They want 99.9 p95 for chat during peak and model pinning control. Product is pushing a new analytics dashboard for next sprint.
liam: That's a big ask. If we score with RICE: reach = medium, impact = high (enterprise), confidence = 60%, effort = high. Rough RICE ~ 38.
sara: Ops data shows rising toil around cache invalidation. If we don't tackle infra debt, adding dashboard will increase oncall noise.
mike: Proposal: 1-sprint spike to quantify effort. Spike goals: refactor prefix/KV cache, add model-routing fallback, run perf benchmarks. Deliverables: bench results, simple canary config, updated runbook.
emma: Count me +1. Product is willing to deprioritize dashboard if we can produce clear numbers. Estimate: 3 eng days + 2 SRE days for a focused spike.
anna: Suggest concrete launch criteria for follow-up work: p95 < 200ms on standard chat payload at 99.9 availability, error-rate delta < 0.1% post-change, no increase in cold-start latency > 50ms, and runbook + rollback steps documented.
liam: Also add acceptance metric for cost impact: token-cost per 1k requests shouldn't increase > 5% on average after any new caching config.
mike: Quick benchmark command for spike: ```./bench --model gpt-open-16k --payload samples/conv.json --concurrency 20 --kv-cache on > spike-results.log``` Please capture p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies.
emma: Can we reuse existing canary infra? deploy-bot: Canary created: canary/slo-spike-2026 started by liam at sha abc123.
sara: For prioritization framework, I propose buckets: emergency SLO fixes (RICE>50), high-value spikes (RICE 30-50), and backlog features (<30). This lands in bucket 2.
mike: If product defers dashboard, we can schedule spike next sprint. Tagging as priority:high and allocating 5 eng-days.
emma: I'll bring this to roadmap sync. If product cuts dashboard, we commit to the spike and put follow-up implementation on the next release track. Thanks all :thumbsup:
